parts:
Dear Jürgen,

I simply try to run the recordTable function using the provided example:

rec.db.species0 <- recordTable(inDir  = wd_images_ID,
                               IDfrom = "directory")

The indir seems to be correct: "C:/Program Files/R/R-3.3.3/library/camtrapR/pictures/sample_images"
But I still get the following error message when I run the recordTable function:

Warning: timeZone is not specified. Assuming UTC
Warning: StationA contains no images;  found 8 JPEGs
Warning: StationB contains no images;  found 23 JPEGs
Warning: StationC contains no images;  found 37 JPEGs
Error: something went wrong. I looked through all those 3 folders and now your table is empty. Did you exclude too many species? Or were date/time information not readable?
In addition: Warning messages:
1: running command 'exiftool -q -f -t -r -Directory -FileName -EXIF:DateTimeOriginal -HierarchicalSubject -ext JPG "C:/Program Files/R/R-3.3.3/library/camtrapR/pictures/sample_images/StationA"' had status 2

I'm not sure this explain the error, but this is rather strange to me that there are warning saying contradictory information (no images vs. "found 8 JPEGs")...

Thank you for your help and your great work!

Kevin

Hi Kevin,
than looks good from what I can see. While you don't run the newest version of R I don't think that should be an issue here.

Can you try running the folliwig code please? It will attempt to extract metadata from the sample images.

# list files
wd_images_ID <- system.file("pictures/sample_images", package = "camtrapR", lib.loc = .libPaths())
file_names <- list.files(wd_images_ID, recursive = TRUE, full.names = TRUE)

head(file_names)

# extract metadata from first image
system(paste('exiftool "', file_names[1], '"', sep = ""))

Cheers,
Jürgen

messages.author: 0b86ca0cb4b615b0
messages.subject: Re: recordTable issue
parts:
Hi Kevin,
R can find the files in the directory, hence all those file names are returned. Exiftool seems to be installed correctly and the system can find it.
But exiftool cannot access the information in the sample images (hence the warning message and no output). To my knowledge, status 2 means that the system could not find the specified file (see here).

But in your sessionInfo it says you run R 3.3.3, whereas the sample images (and camtrapR) are in the library of R 3.4.4. Are you running R in RStudio? If so, can you change the version of R that is run by default to 3.4.4 (Tools - Global Options - General) and see if it changes anything?
If you run R as a standalone program, does it make a difference whether you run version 3.3.3 or 3.4.4? Do you get the same error in both?

I'm sorry, this is mostly guesswork. I don't understand the issue yet.
Best,
Jürgen
